name: Directus secure template with API-aware defaults

settings.CORS_ALLOW_METHODS: GET, POST, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
settings.KEEP_UPSTREAM_HEADERS: Content-Security-Policy Strict-Transport-Security X-Frame-Options X-Content-Type-Options Referrer-Policy Access-Control-Allow-Origin Access-Control-Allow-Credentials Access-Control-Allow-Headers Access-Control-Allow-Methods Access-Control-Expose-Headers Access-Control-Max-Age

steps.title: Web service - Front service
steps.subtitle: Point the template at your Directus hostname(s).

steps.title: Web service - Upstream server
steps.subtitle: Direct the reverse proxy at Directus and keep long-lived requests alive. Buffering stays off so realtime and large asset transfers stream through.

steps.title: HTTP - Directus API constraints
steps.subtitle: Allow the REST verbs Directus uses and keep both body limits above your largest payload. MAX_CLIENT_SIZE also drives ModSecurity's SecRequestBodyLimit.

steps.title: HTTP - Cross-origin access
steps.subtitle: Only needed for a decoupled front end. Replace the origin with your app's own; never pair a wildcard with credentials.

steps.title: Security - Rate and connection limits
steps.subtitle: Directus admin app fans out many parallel requests per page, so the limits sit well above BunkerWeb defaults.

steps.title: Security - Bad behavior
steps.subtitle: 401, 403 and 404 are dropped from the counted codes: Directus returns them on every anonymous or permission-denied API call.

steps.title: Security - Headers and exposure
steps.subtitle: Directus ships its own CSP for the admin app, so the upstream headers are kept and BunkerWeb's policy stays report-only.

steps.title: Performance - Client optimisation
steps.subtitle: Compress proxied API responses; static files are served by Directus, not BunkerWeb.
